concepts.definition: A reporting framework version groups requirements and technical deliverables for specified reference dates. Version number alone does not determine whether an individual module is applicable.
A specific reporting collection within the framework. Modules and their versions are linked to taxonomy entry points and reporting sets.
A structured reporting template represented using axes, ordinates, and combinations of coordinates to derive cell-level data requirements.
The X, Y and where applicable Z structure of a table; the axes contain ordinates such as columns, rows or sheets.
An element at a row, column or sheet location, annotated with properties describing data requirements. Coordinates combine to define the semantics of a cell.
An individually defined reporting fact whose meaning is identified by a combination of dimensional/property characteristics and a metric.
A quantitative or other measurement concept associated with a data type; historically described as a special dimension of the DPM vocabulary.
A property/category used to qualify what a data point represents (for example counterparty sector).
The collection of allowed concept values or members that share a semantic nature; some domains are open, while others are restricted.
A value or item belonging to a domain and used in the categorisation of a variable/data point (for example central banks within a counterparty sector).
A grouping or parent-child organisation of members, used for subsets and sometimes aggregation relationships.
A logical or arithmetic consistency requirement published with the reporting framework. Rule status may change through quarterly EBA packages.
A machine-readable implementation of DPM concepts, constraints and reporting entry points in XBRL / applicable reporting syntax.
